# fun

Jokes, cows, reminders and other things that make a terminal feel like home. Nothing here runs at load time.

## `fun_cow_tweet`

## `fun_flip_copy`

```

```

## `fun_mascot`

Print the name of a randomly chosen cowsay cowfile. Portable: asks cowsay itself for the list instead of the original's `brew list --version` + hardcoded Cellar path, which only worked on an Intel Mac with Homebrew, inside a file that was written on Linux.

**Usage**

```sh
fun_mascot
```

**Examples**

```sh
cowsay -f "$(fun_mascot)" moo
```

**Requires** `cowsay`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/fun.sh:128`](../../modules/common/fun.sh#L128)

## `fun_remind`

Nag yourself later. Sleeps in the background, then notifies. Renamed from `remind`, which is a real binary on Debian and Arch.

**Usage**

```sh
fun_remind in <duration> <message>...
```

**Examples**

```sh
fun_remind in 30m i need to start studying
fun_remind
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/fun.sh:200`](../../modules/common/fun.sh#L200)

## `fun_sudo_last`

Re-run the previous command under sudo. Inspired by https://twitter.com/kathyra_/status/1160810013113237504

> **⚠ DANGER** — Runs your last command as root. The original alias `damn_it='sudo $(fc -ln -1)'` did this instantly, with no echo of what it was about to run and no confirmation — so a typo'd or half-remembered previous command went straight to root. This version prints the command and waits for an explicit yes.

**Usage**

```sh
fun_sudo_last
```

**Examples**

```sh
fun_sudo_last
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/fun.sh:107`](../../modules/common/fun.sh#L107)
